item.title: College Football Playoff officially expanding to 24 teams in 2027, eliminating SEC Championship Game
item.description: While many college football fans are disappointed by the recent news, it was announced Monday that the College Football Playoff will expand to 24 teams in 2027 , with conference championship games being eliminated. ESPN and the CFP have agreed to a five-year deal worth nearly $1.7 billion. ESPN’s Pete Thamel also reported that the network will pay an additional $345 million per year for the expanded 24-team playoff. “A formal agreement between the CFP and ESPN regarding future media rights in connection with potential expansion is in the final stages of review by the CFP,” the Nov. 6 statement read. “A decision on the agreement will be made following this review. We will provide additional updates when appropriate.” With the expansion, college football playoff games could be played on weeknights. On3 also reports that the first- and second-round games will continue to be played at campus sites. After that, teams will compete at bowl sites for the quarterfinals and beyond. This is certainly good news for Kentucky fans, as the Wildcats will have a better opportunity to reach the College Football Playoff and potentially host a game at Kroger Field in the years to come. Kentucky head coach Will Stein even addressed the possibility earlier this season. “Everybody says the (regular season) games aren’t going to matter. Really? I think that’s a really lame take, to be honest. As far as I know, every game in College Football is going to matter.” He later added: “You telling me you wouldn’t want a Playoff game at Kroger Field? I think those takes are bad.” While plenty of fans, including some in Big Blue Nation, are unhappy with the changes, the expanded format will give Kentucky and other programs a greater opportunity to compete for a national championship in the years ahead. However, one major downside for Kentucky fans is that the Wildcats no longer have the opportunity to win an SEC Championship through the conference title game. While the expanded playoff could create more opportunities for Kentucky, it also means saying goodbye to one of the biggest games on the SEC schedule.

item.title: FAMU basketball struggles from free-throw line in blowout loss at UAB
item.description: Florida A&M men’s basketball was an ice-cold 8-for-23 from the free-throw line on Monday. It was the main culprit in the Rattlers’ (0-3) 92-64 loss while visiting the University of Alabama at Birmingham (2-1) at Bartow Arena. FAMU guard Jaden Kempson continues to cement himself as the top-scoring option, leading with a game-high 24 points and also leading the team with seven rebounds. Forward Daisean Williford followed with 11 points, and freshman guard Jayden Joseph had 10. UAB had two leading scorers, with guard tandem Justyn Fernandez and Deuce Jones scoring 20 apiece. The Rattlers actually outshot the UAB Blazers from the field. FAMU made 45% of its shots while UAB shot 41%. The difference was from three. The Rattlers shot 6-for-22, 27%, while the Blazers were 12-for-24, 50%. UAB also won the rebound battle 49-33 and forced 13 FAMU turnovers compared to eight of its own. The Blazers led by as much as 31 points. Next for the Rattlers is a trip to Central Florida for the Showdown in St. Pete . FAMU faces Missouri-Kansas City (1-2) on Wednesday at noon inside the McArthur Center on Eckerd College’s campus. The game will be on YouTube. The UMKC Roos lost to Jacksonville 79-61 on Monday. item.title: Illinois basketball must fix one major issue to beat Texas Tech
item.description: The Illini have started the season 2-0 with blowout victories over Fairleigh Dickinson and Penn inside the State Farm Center. However, Tuesday night in Lubbock will present their first major test of the season. The matchup will feature two top-20 teams inside United Supermarkets Arena and has the potential to be one of the best games of the young season. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: Illinois held off Texas Tech 81-77 in the first meeting between the two teams last season in Champaign. That victory set the tone for the Illini’s season and provided them with a valuable Quad 1 win. A similar opportunity will be on the line in Tuesday night’s rematch. Unfortunately, JT Toppin and David Mirkovic will not be in action Tuesday night. A matchup between the two big men would have been exciting to watch, as both are expected to be All-American candidates if they play enough games this season. Despite playing on the road in a hostile environment, Illinois enters the matchup as a 1.5-point favorite. Limiting turnovers will be the biggest key for the Illini if they want to leave Lubbock with a victory. Illinois had one of the best offenses in the country last season and has looked like an offensive juggernaut once again this year. The Illini are averaging 116 points per game through their first two contests and currently rank No. 1 nationally in adjusted offensive efficiency, according to KenPom. They should be able to continue that offensive success against Texas Tech, but taking care of the basketball will be critical against the Red Raiders. The Illini were one of the best teams in the country at taking care of the ball last season, but that has not been the case through their first two games this year. The increase in turnovers could be a byproduct of playing at a much faster pace, but finding a balance between pushing the tempo and protecting the basketball will be important moving forward. Illinois committed 19 turnovers against Penn on Thursday night, and that number will need to improve against a much tougher Texas Tech defense. According to Bart Torvik, the Red Raiders rank No. 5 nationally in adjusted defensive efficiency and No. 2 in turnover percentage. Meanwhile, Illinois ranks just No. 120 nationally in offensive turnover percentage. That is a significant drop from last season, when the Illini finished the year ranked No. 8 in the country. Freshman guards Ethan Brown and Quentin Coleman will be playing in their first true road games at the collegiate level. item.title: Rebounding saves Indiana against Syracuse, but the offense could use some work
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 9: Bryce Lindsay #2 of the Indiana Hoosiers and Ryan Moesch #0 of the Syracuse Orange reach for a loose ball during the second half at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on November 9, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images This version of Indiana men’s basketball, the second team of the Darian DeVries era, is built just about entirely around its ability to rebound the basketball. DeVries said so multiple times throughout the offseason and Indiana’s strength and physicality was on full display throughout its preseason exhibition run. It didn’t need all that against Eastern Illinois or Bellarmine because it had enough talent to overwhelm those teams on both ends. So it’s a bit interesting how crucial that was in these Hoosiers’ first game that counts against a high-major opponent. Indiana just eked out an 83-80 win over a Syracuse team playing its first season under new head coach Gerry McNamara. It was a close one for about all forty minutes, with neither team managing an extended run. Indiana spent 16:03 leading while Syracuse spent 18:28. Indiana’s largest lead was the 5-point margin it held in the final twelve seconds while Syracuse’s was 7 points about midway through the first half. Syracuse made the most of its time with the ball though, shooting 50.9% from the field and 42.1% from 3. Indiana did not, shooting 41.9% from the field and 36% from 3. It’s just that the Hoosiers ended up taking seven more shots than the Orange because they won the rebounding battle 37-28, turning 14 offensive rebounds into 12 second chance points. Under ideal circumstances, Indiana’s rebounding allows it to overwhelm opponents while building up a strong lead, not stick around in a game where it’s having trouble scoring the ball. Indiana had the most trouble in the first half when the Hoosiers shot just 37.1% from the field and went 3-14 from 3. Darren Harris, who finished the game tying the team lead with 20 points, went 0-4 from deep in the first 20 minutes. It’s good that the Hoosiers found their way in the second half, but the difference was going 6-11 from deep. That’s not even mentioning the defensive woes from this one as Syracuse just kept finding ways to score to build or maintain a lead while keeping Indiana from building one of its own. The Orange found enough favorable mismatches to stay competitive while the Hoosiers’ shots were falling, something that can’t happen too often this year. It’s good that Indiana’s identity led to a win. It still has a few things to figure out, namely offensive efficiency to keep this performance from turning into a trend. Join the conversation! item.title: Why was Barcelona’s Karim Adeyemi left out of latest Germany squad by Jurgen Klopp?
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Karim Adeyemi of FC Barcelona celebrate the victory during the Spanish League, LaLiga EA Sports, football match between Atletico de Madrid and FC Barcelona at Riyadh Air Metropolitano stadium on November 08, 2026, in Madrid, Spain. (Photo By Oscar J. Barroso/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images Karim Adeyemi was surprisingly left out of Jürgen Klopp’s Germany squad , and one ex-Klopp player thinks he knows why. Former goalkeeper Roman Weidenfeller, who played most of his career with Borussia Dortmund, gave his take on the TV show Sky Triple – Der Hagedorn-Fußballtalk. “Karim reacted too late when it came to tracking back to defend. And that is something Jürgen Klopp really doesn’t like,” the former goalkeeper said. Adeyemi was criticized for his lack of defensive workrate against Greece, in a shock 1-0 defeat at home for the Germans. “With Jürgen, you always have full freedom to attack, but you have to be willing to track back to defend,” Weidenfeller explained. The goalkeeper spent seven seasons under Klopp’s orders at Borussia Dortmund, in addition to winning the FIFA World Cup as a substitute for Germany. “I think it’s those little details that end up bothering Jürgen, which might explain why he wasn’t called up. Perhaps it’s a bit of a wake-up call.” Adeyemi has also received reduced playing time since making the move to FC Barcelona last summer. TV pundit Dietmar Hamann disagreed with Klopp’s decision to leave the winger out. “The situation with Adeyemi surprises me. I would have liked for him to be included. There aren’t many players with that kind of speed,” he said.

item.description: The Detroit Red Wings are running out of time to settle the future of Simon Edvinsson , and a new report suggests interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has plenty of teams willing to discuss a potential trade. With the 23-year-old defenseman still unsigned, the situation appears to be moving toward a critical decision. According to a November 9 report from The Fourth Period , Horcoff remains engaged in trade conversations involving Edvinsson, with six NHL teams specifically identified as interested parties. However, despite the ongoing discussions, there is no indication that a deal is close to being completed. item.title: Claiming Crown At Churchill Downs Offers $1.25 Million In Purse Money
item.description: For the third consecutive year Churchill Downs will host the Claiming Crown, a showcase of blue collar runners competing for their share of $1.25 million. Coady Photography The Kentucky Derby and Triple Crown offers much excitement to Thoroughbred racing. The Breeders Cup and those world championships also are huge days in the sport of kings. Although it is much lesser known and publicized, The Claiming Crown is also one of those very important events on the racing calendar. Hosted by Churchill Downs, this Crown is all about the American Dream and the hard work of the everyday hard-working life in horse racing. The Claiming Crown Rewards Those That Are The Foundation Of Racing A definition of the Claiming Crown is necessary before elaborating on the importance of the event. For those that did not realize, all of the Thoroughbred races contested have conditions. This means, in order to enter your horse in a race, they must meet the conditions of the event. For instance, the only condition for the Kentucky Derby is, you must be a three-year old. Other races have much more specific requirements for entry such as, three-year olds and up that have not won two races this year and have started for a claiming price of $12,000 or less. These conditions are written to ensure runners of a competitive nature are matched up so as to level the playing field. To put it in simpler terms, high school football players play against other high schoolers, not junior pro kids, and not NFL players. One of the focal points of Thoroughbred racing has always been the claiming races. Most all race cards feature these events and these “horse trading” races are one of the foundations of the game. Entering a horse in these type races allows for people to buy and sell proven runners that have made it to the track in the afternoon. For those wishing to purchase, their claim must be filed before the race and before the horse changes ownership a post-race veterinary inspection is required. Many stables are built with these types of runners and as horses win and gain notoriety, they no longer run in these races as owners want to hold on to their more valuable commodities. Also, most of these claiming races do not feature large amounts of purse money for horsemen that are running an entrant for a tag. Now, the importance of this event called the Claiming Crown. In 1989, the National Horsemen’s Benevolent and Protective Association (HBPA) and Thoroughbred Owners and Breeders Association launched this event with eyes on rewarding those “blue collar” runners and trainers with an opportunity to run in races with much larger purses. Each event will have starter allowance conditions for horses that have run in claiming races, however each race carries at least a $100,000 purse. item.description: Oct 18, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Guardians pitcher Parker Messick (77) pitches against the Tampa Bay Rays during the first inning at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Cleveland Guardians left-handed starting pitcher Parker Messick has finished in second place for the American League Rookie of the Year Award as the league’s best rookie. Detroit Tigers shortstop/third baseman Kevin McGonigle received 28 out of 30 first-place votes to win the award. McGonigle entered the season as a consensus top three prospect in the sport. Messick received the other two first-place votes and 25 second-place votes, which easily secured a second-place finish for him over the Red Sox’s starting pitcher Payton Tolle and the White Sox’s first baseman Munetaka Murakami . Teammate Chase DeLauter also received a second-place vote and finished sixth overall in the voting. The 25-year-old pitcher produced 4.9 fWAR in 186 1/3 innings, which ranked fourth overall in the AL. Messick limited opponents to a 2.56 ERA (3.07 FIP) while starting 32 games for the Guardians. He struck out 25.8% of batters, and his 6.6% walk rate ranked in the top ten in the AL. Per Baseball Savant’s Pitching Run Value, his +26 PRV ranked in the 98th percentile amongst all pitchers. He found success in limiting barrels and hard hits. His barrel rate of 5% ranked in the 88th percentile, while his hard-hit rate of 34.3% ranked in the 80th percentile. Previous winners of the AL Rookie of the Year Award include Oakland Athletics’ first baseman Nick Kurtz (2025), New York Yankees’ pitcher Luis Gil (2024), and Baltimore Orioles’ shortstop Gunnar Henderson (2023). Messick joins a list of Cleveland winners, such as Sandy Alomar (1990), Joe Charboneau (1980), Chris Chambliss (1971), and Herb Score (1955). Parker Messick Drafted in 2022, Debuted Last Season Messick was drafted in the second round of the 2022 draft by the Guardians. He debuted in the majors last year and produced a 2.72 ERA (2.98 FIP) in 39 2/3 innings. The threshold for innings pitched for a pitcher to retain their rookie eligibility is 50 innings, which is why Messick was still considered a rookie in his second year in the majors. He struck out 38 batters and walked six while starting in seven games. Messick has six pitches in his repertoire. He relies on his four-seam fastball, which causes fits for right-handed hitters (+19 PRV). Overall, his four-seamer produced a .186/.248/.295 slash line and had a 25.1% whiff rate. His changeup and sinker also yielded +6 PRV against right-handers. He can mix in a curveball, slider, and a cutter, but with less efficiency. In his first taste of the playoffs in 2026, he uncharacteristically walked ten batters in 13 2/3 innings while striking out 17. He would finish with a 3.95 ERA (3.98 FIP) in four starts. item.title: Lakers get a major boost from an unexpected source in sixth straight victory
item.description: ATLANTA — The Lakers didn’t need Luka Dončić to continue his 40-point scoring streak to leave Starm Farm Arena with a victory on Monday night. Even with Austin Reaves sidelined because of an illness fresh off scoring a season-high 43 points in Sunday’s win over the Pistons, the Lakers didn’t need Dončić to perform at the unrealistically high he set for himself externally over the last two weeks. Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket against the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. NBAE via Getty Images They just needed the Slovenian superstar to make the plays in front of him that the Hawks were conceding – which he did to the tune of 32 points, 10 assists and 8 rebounds for a near triple-double in the Lakers’ 124-114 win over the Hawks to push the team’s winning streak to six games. Dončić added five steals and 2 blocked shots during a night he stuffed the stat sheet while his non-Reaves teammates picked up the scoring slack with the league’s No. 11 scorer sidelined. Sandro Mamukelashvili stepped up the most, scoring a season-high 23 points on 7-for-13 shooting (5 of 8 on 3-pointers), finding his spots within the offense to be a scorer and distributor in a way the Lakers needed without their second-best playmaker. Sandro Mamukelashvili of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a 3-point basket against the Atlanta Hawks in Atlanta on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Collin Sexton provided the biggest jolt off the bench, with his 18 points and 6 assists coming at critical moments. Sexton also assisted Walker Kessler (21 points, 10 rebounds, 4 assists) on three alley-oops to get the starting big man going early. The Lakers quickly reversed their slow start, turning an early 15-7 deficit into a 31-22 lead going into the second quarter, with their lead growing to as many as 20 points midway through the quarter. Los Angeles Lakers guard Collin Sexton (10) reacts during the first half of an NBA Cup basketball game against the Atlanta Hawks in Atlanta, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. AP Photo/Mike Stewart Monday played out similarly as Sunday, with the Hawks threatening to erase the Lakers’ lead but never tying or getting ahead of the game. The Lakers closed the game out with a 9-3 run, with Dončić and Mamukelashvili at the heart of creating the easy offense the team is getting used to benefiting from. The Lakers improved to 10-2 on the season with the victory. They’ll travel to Milwaukee to play the Bucks on Wednesday.
